a: Suspending a journal with an active journal inside it leaves that inner journal writing while the history counts no journal open
The parent history's `apply` / `applyOps` / `recordEntry` run under an active journal, while `undo`/`redo`/`goto` refuse
A `selection.set` that throws during undo/redo leaves the entry on a stack its ops have already left
A restored snapshot with an empty branch makes `branches()` and `switchBranch()` throw TypeError
`createSwapOp`'s inverse has no `name`/`args`, so an observed undo reports applied ops that can't be identified or replayed
A goto whose return walk also throws moves the stacks and bumps the version without telling `observe`
`restore` keeps a future id from colliding with the restored entries but not with the restored floor or branch fork points
b: Suspending a journal leaves a journal opened inside it active, so the history accepts undo and a second journal while that child still writes
A raw history's apply, applyOps, recordEntry, clear, restore, prune, dropRedo and switchBranch do not refuse while a journal is active, so an entry can land beneath a journal's later commit
Canceling a journal unwinds its children in the order they were created, not the order their edits ran
`History.undo`/`redo` skip the journal refusal when their stack is empty
`restore` bumps `nextEntryId` past every restored entry id but not past `floor` or a branch's `at`, so a new entry can take the floor's id
`createSwapOp`'s inverse has no `name` or `args`, so an observed undo of a swap reports an anonymous op
